How to change your Wi-Fi password

  1. Open your router's admin page — usually 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1, or the address on the sticker under the router — and sign in. Your provider's app may do the same job.
  2. Find the wireless (WLAN) settings and choose WPA2-Personal or WPA3-Personal, or the mixed WPA2/WPA3 mode if you have older devices.
  3. Paste the password generated above and save. Every device disconnects; reconnect them with the new password or by scanning the QR code.
  4. While you are there, change the router's own admin password if it is still the default.

Which style to choose

  • 20 letters and digits — about 111 bits, far beyond brute force, and with no look-alike characters, so typing it on a TV remote is bearable.
  • 5 random words — about 68 bits and easy to read out to a visitor. A WPA2 handshake can be attacked offline, so do not go below five words.
  • 32 characters with symbols or 63 characters — for networks no human types: smart-home gadgets, or an office network everyone joins with the QR code.

Is sharing Wi-Fi by QR code safe?

The QR code is simply the network name and password in a standard text format (WIFI:T:WPA;S:…;P:…;;) that phone cameras understand. Anyone who can photograph it can join, so treat a printed card like the password itself — on the fridge, not in the window. For visitors, consider a separate guest network that cannot reach your own devices.

Questions people ask

How long should a Wi-Fi password be?

WPA2 and WPA3 accept 8 to 63 characters. Because a WPA2 handshake can be captured and attacked offline, use at least 16 random characters or 5 random words. WPA3 resists that offline attack, but most networks still let WPA2 devices in.

Does the QR code work on iPhone and Android?

Yes. The built-in camera app recognises Wi-Fi QR codes on iPhone (iOS 11 and later) and on most Android phones (Android 10 and later, or through Google Lens).

Can I make a QR code for the password I already have?

Yes. Type your network name, then replace the generated password with your own. The QR code updates as you type.

Is my network name or password sent anywhere?

No. The password and the QR code are generated in your browser, and the page cannot make network requests. Nothing about your network is stored — only the password style and security type you picked.

WPA2 or WPA3?

Use WPA3 if all your devices support it, otherwise the mixed WPA2/WPA3 mode. Avoid WEP and open networks: WEP can be cracked in minutes. The QR code works the same for WPA2 and WPA3.
